rules.title: Working rules
rules.intro: For approved HugoTeam members. Everything here matches how the system actually works.

sections.title: Time and commitment
items: The rhythm is 5–10 hours a week, arranged around your class schedule. There are no fixed office hours.
HugoTeam is non-profit. This is not employment and there is no salary; what you get is real projects, credit and membership benefits.
If exams, an internship or family matters get in the way, say so in the in-app channel beforehand. Early notice always beats silence and a missed deadline.

sections.title: Taking on work and handing it over
items: Every task moves through four states: assigned → doing → submitted → done. Press Start when you actually begin, rather than leaving a task marked assigned while you work on it quietly.
When you submit, write a short note: what you did, what is still open, where to see the result. That is the first thing the reviewer reads.
Work that does not pass comes back with a comment. Fix it and resubmit on the same task, do not create a new one.
If something blocks you for more than one working session, ask. Asking early is cheaper than redoing the work.

sections.title: Logging hours
items: Log hours on the day you actually worked, between 0.25 and 24 hours per entry. Log them the same day, or by the end of the week at the latest — not in a batch at month end.
Link the hours to a task whenever they belong to one; that is the fastest way to reconcile a discrepancy.
Say what you did. One specific line beats ten vague words.
Hours still awaiting approval can be deleted by you. Approved hours cannot — message us to change those.
Logging hours you did not work is grounds for revoking membership.

sections.title: Communication
items: The main channel is the in-app message box; every message is kept so it can be looked up later.
For anything needing a record, or concerning your account, email contact@hugowishpax.studio from your account address.
The usual response time is within the next working day.

sections.title: Quality and credit
items: The code you write must be yours, or licensed for the use. Copying a block from elsewhere without saying so is a breach.
Never put secret keys, passwords or real user data in the source or in screenshots.
Contributions are credited on GitHub for the part you did.
Internal project data and content stay within the work; they do not leave it.

sections.title: What you get
items: VVIP membership runs for 3 years from your approval date.
The 500 approved-hour mark recognises long-term contribution.
You keep full authorship of what you write and may use it in your portfolio.
